title: svc-proxy-prefetch-and-outlier-pruning-to-cut-tracing-hotpath-costs
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
We’ve observed that tracer hotpath allocations and span metadata marshalling are contributing 1.8–4.0% tail CPU on several high-QPS services. Prior sampling efforts reduced emitted traces but still leave substantial in-hotpath work (headers/kv marshalling, small allocations, locks). The goal of this ticket is to move decision and light prefiltering into the service proxy layer, reduce per-request allocations, and only escalate expensive sampling decisions to a background worker when a request is a candidate for full trace emission.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Lightweight prefetch decision in svc-proxy: compute a small set of deterministic, low-cost heuristics (status code, latency bucket, presence of error flags, route hash) to mark a request as a "trace candidate". This runs with zero allocations and no locks.
2) Sketch-based outlier detector: maintain a compact, ring-based sketch in the proxy to track recent latency distributions per route. If a request is >X sigma from the median or exceeds a p99 threshold, mark for detailed capture. The sketch is optimized for write-only hotpath and small memory.
3) Defer heavy work: when a candidate is found, enqueue a tiny sampling token to a bounded lock-free queue shared with an async worker (background tracer flusher). The worker performs span encoding, attribute enrichment, and final sampling (reservoir/tail decisions) off the request thread.
4) Nullable span headers: include a two-byte sampling token in the request flow; only when the worker confirms emission do we allocate full span buffers and attach them to the outbound collector. This avoids span object lifetimes on non-candidate requests.
5) Safety net and fallbacks: if the queue is filled, fallback to probabilistic light-sample emission (very small, fixed-size) to avoid dropping all signals. Also provide a per-route opt-out for routes that require full tracing (admins).

Experimental results (prototype):
- Test environment: prod-like replay against staging traffic for 48h.
- Baseline hotpath cost: ~3.2% CPU contribution to request path (measured by eBPF stacks).
- Prototype with proxy-prefetch + async worker: drop to ~1.0% CPU (approx 69% reduction).
- Trace emission count: emitted traces reduced by 8.7x overall and by 12x for non-error routes.
- Tail capture: prototype retained 96.1% of p99 latency anomalies and 98.4% of error traces (based on labelled incidents in the replay).

Tradeoffs and risks:
- Some rare multi-span causal chains that only manifest later in processing may be missed if not flagged by small heuristics. Mitigation: we add route-level backlog sniffers and a short-term re-check window in the worker.
- Sketch maintenance complexity: bugs can skew p99 thresholds if sketch eviction is wrong. Mitigation: conservative thresholds in canary and detailed histogram exporters.
- Observability regression risk: if rollout occurs too quickly, SREs may lose actionable traces. Rollout plan described below addresses this.

Implementation plan (tasks):
- svc-proxy: add candidate-decider path (low-level C/Go code). Feature-flagged. (PR #8234)
- shared probe: implement ring-sketch with per-route keys. Export sketch metrics to metrics pipeline. (PR #8251)
- tracer-worker: new offload worker binary integrated with existing flusher. Handles final encoding and emission. (PR #8267)
- console/dashboards: add "prefilter sampling" dashboard showing queue drops, prefilter hit-rate, emitted vs expected tail capture.
- e2e tests: heavy replay harness, randomized fuzzing of sketch states, integration with trace replay harness.

Rollout and monitoring:
- Canary stage 1: feature flag enabled on 5% of traffic for 72h. Monitor CPU delta, emitted trace rate, p99 retention, error trace retention, queue drops.
- Canary stage 2: increase to 30% for 7d if metrics stable.
- Stage 3: 100% with opt-outs for critical routes.
- Rollback criteria: >10% regression in alerting rate for SLOs tied to latency detection, >5% increase in undetected errors per support tickets, or >2x queue overflow rate.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Proxy+Prefetch+and+Sketch+Outlier+Design
- Prototype PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8234, https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8251, https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8267
- Staging dashboard (Observability): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/obs/proxy-prefetch-canary
- Load test results: gs://redwood-artifacts/obs/proxy-prefetch/2026-03-08-results.html

Review notes and feedback so far:
- PM (Jon Kim): requested quantitative acceptance criteria for p99 retention and an explicit SLO for "no-more-than-5-missed-critical-errors" during canary. Added to acceptance criteria below.
- Design (Priya Rao): suggested adding a small LRU of recently-seen request-ids to catch correlated multi-request traces; decided to postpone to follow-up (ENG-100009) due to complexity.
- SRE (Mikael Lind): asked for a conservative initial threshold and additional alerting for queue saturation. Implemented.

Next steps (short term):
- Complete svc-proxy integration tests and land PR #8234 to canary infra (target: 2026-03-15).
- Wire sketch metrics into console panels and add alert rules for queue_drop_rate and p99_retention (target: 2026-03-18).
- Start 5% canary and collect 72h data.

Longer term follow-ups (separate tickets):
- ENG-100009: LRU correlation buffer for multi-request traces
- ENG-100010: per-tenant adaptive thresholds based on traffic patterns
- ENG-100011: export compact sketch snapshots for offline forensic replays
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath CPU contribution reduced by >=50% relative to baseline in staging replay
Emitted trace count reduced by >=5x for non-error traffic in canary
Retention of p99 latency anomalies >=95% and error trace retention >=97% in canary replay
Queue overflow rate remains <0.1% during canary
Feature flagged with opt-out per-route and rollback plan documented
